job.title: Logistics Support Coordinator
job.description:
Logistics:
Shipping and pulling jobs primarily but may be needed to do some cycle counting as well.

Stock Room:
-Team members have a scanner, a laptop and a cart. There is a board that shows all of the jobs to be picked. The grab the info for the job that needs to be picked, print the paperwork (Pick List) and then go and pull all of the components for the job and place them on a cart. A Pick List can have anywhere from 50 components to 150 components.

Receiving:
-Team Members here sign for deliveries, boxes received are placed on carts. The person here logs the receipts into our system, enters the location they will go into the stock room (via computer) and then goes and places the parts in the appropriate location on the shelves in the stock room.

Shipping:
-Team members are responsible for packing product via customer requirements then use FedEX, UPS, etc to create labels to ship. Some of our customers have portals that authorizations need to be approved. Someone who has shipping internationally (export compliance) would be a plus. We are not looking for someone who has only called freight carriers to pick up pallets (freight) – this is very different from that.

Split Shift Hours: 11:30 am – 8:00 pm
Position requires High School Diploma or GED.
$1,000 Signing Bonus paid as follows: $250 at 30 days, $750 at 6 months

Position Summary
With guidance in a team environment, responsible for Stock Room functions including maintaining a cycle-counting program that validates our inventory counts for accounting and production purposes. Position is also required to perform a variety of product support duties of basic and/or moderate scope while following and assisting in the development of procedures and processes in one or more of the following functions per B00284 (Logistics
– Receiving, Stockroom and Shipping): stockroom, raw stock, parts identification, shipping, receiving, stockroom, clean operations, etc. Initial primary focus is the Stockroom with support in Shipping. Eventually cross training will occur to cover all Logistics positions.
Shipping
· Prepare parts and/or materials to assure safe handling for shipment including the completion of the necessary paperwork and shipping records.
· Prepare packaging per specifications for shipment including computer input for necessary labels, forms and shipping records.
· Interpret shipping instructions as referenced on company documents or customer specifications or standards related to preservation and packing.
· Prepare stencils and mark shipments in a legible manner.
· Prepare air bills, bills of lading and sales order forms for the carrier and company records.
· Contact carriers for dispatching shipments, establishing rates or tracing follow-up information.
Stockroom and Cycle Counting
· Maintain a cycle counting program by counting inventory
· Reconciling inventory counts within our electronic system
· Identify and resolve all inventory issues
· Receive material, check and identify parts by type or part number
· Prepare parts for storage and place stock in proper location as directed.
· Select parts from stock to fill orders according to parts lists.
· Perform cycle inventory count.
· Maintain, update and access necessary records utilizing a computer.
· Responsible for releasing requisitions, editing requisitions, filling shortages and deleting requisitions.
Receiving
· Receive shipments at receiving dock and forward materials to the appropriate team.
· Weigh or count incoming/outbound parts or materials.
· Perform data input to update system records and verify all documents for completeness and accuracy.
Raw Stock
· Receive incoming raw stock and verify material against documentation for identification and accuracy of quantity.
· Load and unload trucks and move raw material to the proper location.
· Identify and code raw materials and operate saw to cut stock to dimensional specifications.
· Perform minor repair of equipment.
· Report critical shortages and/or problems to appropriate organizations.
· Issue jobs per schedule and update shop floor, MRP and other systems.
Parts Identification
· Identify parts using the proper identification methods and equipment indicated by the traveler and/or blueprint.
· Client out exact dimensions and locations on the parts for identification markings.
Clean Operations
· Observe all prescribed safety rules and maintain a neat and orderly, FOD free work area.

Additional Responsibilities
· Actively participate in department problem solving, lean events and high-performance teams.
· Actively maintain 5S in the department.

Job Qualifications
  • Must possess a High School Diploma or equivalent
  • Minimum of one year related product support experience and demonstrated ability to perform described position responsibilities.
  • May be required to be operate moving equipment and saw equipment and meet OSHA safety qualifications.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include the ability to favorably pass a visual acuity exam (which includes far vision, near vision and color perception)
  • May require forklift operator certificate.
  • Good level of knowledge and experience with computers including software packages and mainframe systems.
  • Must demonstrate manual dexterity.
  • Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations.
  • Ability to read and understand related forms and specifications.
  • May be required to lift up to 50 lbs.
  • Must demonstrate effective verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with others and be a participative team player.
  • May be required to post and report on Team Improvement Board metrics.

Benefits:
  • Competitive Medical with prescription, Dental (including orthodontia) & Vision from date of hire
  • Supplemental Medical Benefits: Critical Illness, Accidental Injury and Hospital Indemnity
  • Life insurance policy – Parker paid
  • Annual Cash Incentive Plan (bonus)
  • 401K with 5% company match
  • 13 Paid Holidays
  • Education (tuition) Reimbursement Program
  • Employee Recognition Program/Events & Community Service Opportunities

job.title: Litigation Paralegal - Hybrid Work Schedule
job.description:
Litigation Paralegal – Jacksonville, FL

Direct Hire | Hybrid Schedule – 3 Days in Office / 2 Days Remote

Nesco Resource is recruiting an experienced Litigation Paralegal for one of our established law firm clients in Jacksonville, FL. This is a direct hire opportunity offering a hybrid work schedule, with three days in the office and two days working from home.

Our client is seeking a proactive, highly organized Litigation Paralegal to support attorneys across a variety of litigation matters. The ideal candidate will have a strong background working in a litigation law firm, excellent organizational and calendaring skills, and the ability to manage a large caseload in a fast-paced environment.

Candidates should have a working knowledge of federal and state court rules, procedures, and electronic filing systems, along with experience conducting legal research using LexisNexis and/or Westlaw.

Key Responsibilities

  • Draft routine court documents, including Notices of Appearance, Pro Hac Vice Motions, Notices of Motion, Subpoenas, Stipulations, and other legal filings.

  • Prepare and compile legal documents, discovery responses, affidavits, and supporting materials for attorney review.

  • Request, subpoena, and coordinate with record vendors to obtain medical treatment and educational records.

  • Prepare exhibits and demonstrative evidence for hearings, depositions, and trials.

  • Conduct legal research using LexisNexis, Westlaw, and public access websites to support litigation defense strategies.

  • Organize, analyze, summarize, and index medical records, educational records, and other case-related documents.

  • Assist attorneys with witness preparation for depositions and trials.

  • Review documents for relevance and privilege in preparation for disclosure.

  • Analyze and categorize reports, discovery responses, and other case materials.

  • Maintain accurate case files, deadlines, scheduling, and court calendars.

  • Capture and record billable time in accordance with firm policies and procedures.

Qualifications

  • 4+ years of relevant litigation paralegal experience, preferably within a law firm.

  • Strong organizational, communication, scheduling, and follow-up skills.

  • Experience managing multiple attorneys, competing deadlines, and document-intensive cases.

  • Knowledge of federal and state court procedures and electronic filing systems.

  • Proficiency in LexisNexis and/or Westlaw, Microsoft Word, Excel, and KOFAX Professional.

  • Experience preparing medical chronologies and billing indexes preferred.

  • Bachelor's degree and/or Paralegal Certificate.

  • Ability to work independently while maintaining a collaborative, team-oriented approach.

  • Strong attention to detail, accuracy, and professionalism.

Schedule & Work Arrangement

  • Employment Type: Direct Hire

  • Location: Jacksonville, FL

  • Hybrid Schedule: 3 days in office / 2 days remote

  • Hours: Monday–Friday, 8:30 AM–5:30 PM, including a one-hour lunch

  • Overtime: Flexibility to work additional hours when needed

About the Opportunity

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Litigation Paralegal who enjoys working on a variety of cases, supporting multiple attorneys, and taking ownership of their work. Our client values individuals who are dependable, detail-oriented, quick learners, and committed to producing high-quality work.

Interested candidates are encouraged to apply through Nesco Resource to learn more about this opportunity.

  • Document repairs, PMs, work orders, labor, parts, and equipment issues.

job.title: NDT Technician II
job.description:
RPO Direct Hire

Full-time day shift in an hourly position - 7am - 4:00pm
Must be UT and FPI certified.

Position Summary
The Level II Nondestructive Testing (NDT) Technician is responsible for performing and interpreting Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (FPI) and Ultrasonic Testing (UT) on aerospace components and assemblies in accordance with applicable customer, industry, and company specifications. The technician will independently conduct inspections, evaluate results, document findings, and ensure product compliance while maintaining a safe and efficient work environment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Perform Level II Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection (FPI) on aerospace components and hardware in accordance with approved procedures and specifications.
Perform Level II Ultrasonic Testing (UT) inspections, including setup, calibration, testing, and evaluation of inspection results.
Interpret and evaluate inspection indications in accordance with acceptance and rejection criteria.
Prepare and maintain inspection reports, records, certifications, and related documentation.
Verify equipment calibration and perform daily system performance checks.
Ensure compliance with NAS410, customer specifications, and company procedures.
Review work instructions, blueprints, engineering drawings, and technical specifications.
Identify and segregate nonconforming material and initiate required documentation.
Support internal, customer, and regulatory audits as required.
Assist with the training and mentoring of Level I technicians and trainees.
Maintain cleanliness and organization of NDT equipment and work areas.
Follow all safety, environmental, and quality requirements.

Required Qualifications
Current or previously certified Level II in FPI and UT in accordance with NAS410, SNT-TC-1A, or equivalent employer-based certification program.
High school diploma or GED required.
Minimum of 3 years of NDT inspection experience, preferably in aerospace manufacturing.
Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and process instructions.
Working knowledge of NDT standards, procedures, and quality system requirements.
Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Office and inspection reporting systems.

Preferred Qualifications
Aerospace manufacturing experience.
Additional NDT certifications (MT, ET, RT, VT, etc.).
Experience with customer specifications from major aerospace OEMs.
Familiarity with NADCAP requirements and audits.
Physical Requirements
Ability to stand, walk, bend, and lift up to 35 pounds throughout the shift.
Ability to distinguish colors and contrast as required for FPI evaluations.
Visual acuity sufficient to perform inspections and interpret indications.
Ability to work in manufacturing and laboratory environments.
Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE).

Work Environment
Manufacturing and inspection laboratory setting.
Exposure to chemicals used in penetrant inspection processes.
Frequent interaction with production, engineering, and quality personnel.
Overtime and weekend work may be required based on business needs.
Key Competencies
Attention to Detail
Technical Aptitude
Problem Solving
Quality Focus
Communication Skills
Teamwork
Safety Awareness
Integrity and Professionalism

job.title: Process Engineer II
job.description:
Job Title: Process Engineer II
Location: Newton, NC
Schedule: Full-time, Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Work Arrangement: On-site

Position Summary
The Contract Process Engineer II supports manufacturing process qualification, optimization, capacity expansion, and capital projects. This role develops process solutions, analyzes performance data, resolves technical issues, and supports project execution from design through commissioning and closeout.
Working with production, maintenance, quality, R&D, EHS, automation, project management, vendors, and contractors, the engineer improves safety, quality, yield, capacity, reliability, and cost performance.

Key Responsibilities
  • Support equipment upgrades, process development/modifications, and continuous-improvement initiatives from design through startup and performance verification.
  • Qualify, evaluate, troubleshoot, and optimize manufacturing processes, equipment, workflows, and operating conditions.
  • Prepare and maintain engineering documentation, process descriptions, equipment specifications, calculations, reports, and operating procedures.
  • Conduct process calculations, equipment-sizing evaluations, capacity studies, process simulations, and statistical data analysis.
  • Support process recipe creation, testing, validation, and process integration.
  • Partner with project managers to define scope, manage technical risks, track progress, and support schedules, estimates, and corrective actions.
  • Participate in design, process-safety, risk, and management-of-change reviews.
  • Develop and execute commissioning plans, startup procedures, test protocols, and acceptance criteria.
  • Investigate process issues, perform root-cause analysis, and implement corrective actions.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure processes and designs are safe, compliant, operable, and maintainable.
  • Identify and implement improvements using Lean, Six Sigma, DMAIC, DOE, 8D, FMEA, and related methodologies.
  • Prepare trial summaries and present to upper-level managers and stakeholders.

Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Chemical, Mechanical, Process, Electrical, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline.
2+ years of process, manufacturing, or project engineering experience in an industrial or manufacturing environment.
Experience with process improvement, equipment upgrades, process development, or manufacturing operations.
Ability to develop and review process documentation, including PFDs, P&IDs, calculations, and equipment specifications.
Experience supporting construction, commissioning, startup, production troubleshooting, or field activities.
Strong data analytical, problem-solving, organizational, communication, and technical writing skills.
Ability to present statistical data to cross functional teams by using software and appropriate tools
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently in a fast-paced project environment.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and statistical-analysis software, such as JMP.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience with process-design or project-management tools, such as Aspen Plus, HYSYS, AutoCAD Plant 3D, MATLAB, Microsoft Project, or Primavera.
Knowledge of process equipment, instrumentation, automation, PLC, SCADA, DCS, and control systems.
Familiarity with process-safety methods, including HAZOP, What-If, PHA, LOPA, FMEA, and Management of Change.
Knowledge of applicable standards and regulations, including OSHA, NFPA, ASME, API, ISA, EPA, GMP, FDA, or ISO.
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, PE, or EIT certification.

Work Environment
Primarily on-site in office, manufacturing, and construction environments.
Periodic travel to nearby *** sites (10 - 12 min drive) and occasional off-hours support may be required for project activities, shutdowns, commissioning, or startup.

job.title: Capital Project Scheduler - (Refinery)
job.description:
Position Summary

Capital Project Scheduler

We are seeking an experienced Capital Project Scheduler to support large-scale midstream, refining, and industrial capital projects. The Scheduler will be responsible for developing, maintaining, analyzing, and reporting integrated project schedules throughout the full project lifecycle, including engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and startup.

The ideal candidate will have strong hands-on experience with Primavera P6, Critical Path Methodology (CPM), schedule forecasting, risk analysis, contractor schedule review, and capital project execution. This individual will work closely with project management, engineering, procurement, construction, contractors, and project controls teams to ensure projects remain aligned with approved schedules, milestones, and execution plans.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain detailed resource-loaded project schedules using Primavera P6.
  • Build and maintain integrated Level 1 through Level 4 schedules.
  • Establish project baselines and maintain schedule integrity throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Develop schedules covering engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and startup activities.
  • Establish schedule coding structures, calendars, activity attributes, and logic relationships.
  • Facilitate schedule development and planning workshops with project stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operations teams to identify milestones, constraints, and execution requirements.
  • Validate schedule logic, critical path activities, float, and overall schedule health.
  • Collect, validate, and update project progress during established reporting cycles.
  • Analyze schedule performance and forecast project completion dates.
  • Identify schedule trends, productivity impacts, delays, and emerging risks.
  • Perform critical path and near-critical path analysis.
  • Develop recovery schedules and mitigation plans for schedule variances.
  • Review contractor schedules and validate reported progress.
  • Generate weekly and monthly schedule reports for project leadership.
  • Develop dashboards, KPIs, milestone reports, look-ahead schedules, S-curves, and executive summaries.
  • Support earned value management reporting where applicable.
  • Monitor schedule performance indicators including SPI, milestone achievement, float consumption, and schedule health.
  • Participate in schedule risk assessments and support probabilistic schedule analysis and Monte Carlo simulations.
  • Evaluate schedule impacts related to scope changes, delays, contractor performance, change orders, and unforeseen events.
  • Support claims analysis and schedule impact evaluations.
  • Review contractor schedules for compliance with project requirements and execution plans.
  • Ensure schedule integration across multiple contractors, vendors, and project teams.
  • Participate in planning meetings, constructability reviews, project reviews, and turnaround planning activities.
  • Communicate schedule status, risks, impacts, recovery strategies, and forecast dates to project leadership.

Required Qualifications

  • 5–10+ years of project scheduling experience supporting major capital projects.
  • Minimum 5 years of hands-on Primavera P6 experience.
  • Experience supporting capital projects in one or more of the following industries:
    • Refining
    • Midstream
    • Oil & Gas
    • Pipelines
    • Terminals
    • Storage facilities
    • Petrochemical or heavy industrial
  • Experience working with EPC contractors and/or owner organizations.
  • Advanced proficiency with Primavera P6 Professional.
  • Strong understanding of Critical Path Methodology (CPM).
  • Experience with resource loading and cost loading.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills.
  • Experience with Power BI preferred.
  • Knowledge of engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and startup processes.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with project leadership, contractors, vendors, engineering, procurement, and field construction teams.

Preferred Skills

  • Schedule risk analysis
  • Monte Carlo simulation
  • Schedule recovery planning
  • Delay and impact analysis
  • Contractor schedule review
  • Change management
  • Construction sequencing
  • Forecasting and trend analysis
  • Executive reporting and presentations
  • Earned Value Management (EVM)
  • S-Curve and KPI development

Work Environment

This is a 100% onsite position in Dallas, TX. Candidates must be able to work onsite.

job.title: Accounts Receivable Specialist
job.description:
Accounts Receivable Specialist

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Accounts Receivable Specialist to support accounts receivable, collections, cash application, customer account reconciliation, and reporting activities.

This position is responsible for monitoring outstanding receivables, collecting past-due balances, researching payment and invoice discrepancies, maintaining accurate collection documentation, and partnering with internal teams to resolve customer account issues. The role also supports month-end activities, including dock walk audits, monitoring non-invoiced shipments, and other accounting and reporting responsibilities.

The ideal candidate has at least two years of accounts receivable or accounting experience, strong Microsoft Excel skills, experience with ERP or billing systems, and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines within a fast-paced environment.

Work Schedule

  • Shift: 1st Shift

  • Must be available to work two Saturdays per month.

  • Must be available during month-end close, including at minimum the first three business days of each month.

  • Overtime may be required based on business needs, deadlines, and reporting requirements.

  • Must be able to adjust schedule as needed to support month-end and other time-sensitive accounting activities.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Receivable & Collections

  • Support Accounts Receivable collection activities by working with customers, contract administrators, and the A/R team to ensure timely and effective collection efforts.

  • Contact customers via email and phone regarding:

    • Past-due balances

    • Payment status

    • Account balances

    • Invoice discrepancies

    • Disputes

    • Other accounts receivable matters

  • Review A/R aging reports on a daily and weekly basis and take appropriate action on delinquent accounts.

  • Prioritize collection activities based on aging, payment risk, customer history, and business impact.

  • Monitor promises to pay and follow up to ensure customer commitments are met.

  • Maintain accurate notes documenting collection attempts, customer communications, payment commitments, and follow-up activities.

  • Assist with credit hold and release reviews and provide escalation recommendations for high-risk or past-due accounts.

  • Provide management with updates regarding collection efforts, high-risk accounts, dispute status, and expected cash receipts.

Cash Application & Account Reconciliation

  • Support cash application and customer account maintenance activities.

  • Research and resolve:

    • Short payments

    • Deductions

    • Chargebacks

    • Unapplied payments

    • Invoice discrepancies

    • Customer disputes

  • Assist with account reconciliation and payment discrepancy research.

  • Support credit memo and additional billing creation as needed.

  • Ensure transactions and account activity are processed accurately and in accordance with established accounting procedures and internal controls.

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Partner with internal teams including:

    • Sales

    • Customer Service

    • Contracts

    • Operations

    • Shipping

    • Planning

    • Production Support

    • Key Account Managers

  • Coordinate with internal stakeholders to resolve billing, shipping, documentation, and payment issues in a timely manner.

  • Gather and provide customers with supporting documentation as needed, including:

    • Invoices

    • Statements

    • Proof of delivery

    • Shipping documentation

    • Other customer account support

Month-End & Dock Walk Audits

  • Perform monthly dock walk audits on the last business day of each month.

  • Verify shipping boxes and corresponding shipping documentation against the non-invoiced shipper list.

  • Follow up with the Shipping Department regarding boxes or shipments not properly reflected on the list.

  • Verify shipments that have been shipped but not invoiced within the same month.

  • Monitor outstanding non-invoiced shipments and perform necessary follow-up.

  • Support month-end close activities and related accounting deadlines.

Reporting & Accounting Support

  • Prepare and maintain required daily, weekly, and monthly reports.

  • Track non-invoiced work orders and shipments on a weekly basis.

  • Support ad-hoc accounting and reporting projects as required.

  • May assist with additional accounting responsibilities as proficiency is demonstrated, including:

    • Journal entries

    • Account reconciliations

    • Financial and operational reports

    • Other accounting support activities

  • Assist with maintaining compliance with established accounting policies, procedures, and internal controls.

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum of 2 years of relevant Accounts Receivable or accounting experience.

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, ideally in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

  • Strong knowledge of accounts receivable and collection processes.

  • Experience with ERP or billing systems and order-to-cash processes.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including:

    • Pivot Tables

    • VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP

    • INDEX/MATCH

    • Basic formulas

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy in data entry and reconciliation.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Comfortable communicating with external customers and internal Operations, Shipping, Sales, and other business teams.

  • Ability to prioritize workload and manage multiple responsibilities simultaneously.

  • Ability to meet strict deadlines within a fast-paced environment.

  • Strong problem-solving and issue-resolution skills.

  • Ability to follow established procedures and appropriately escalate issues.

  • Reliable and punctual with the ability to work overtime as business needs require.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Microsoft Power BI or similar reporting tools.

  • Previous experience within a manufacturing, distribution, or government contracting environment.

  • Experience supporting month-end accounting activities.

  • Experience with cash application, collections, account reconciliation, and order-to-cash processes.

job.title: Solderer
job.description:
Nesco Resource is looking for Solderers for our long-time client in Rochester Hills, MI. This shift operates Monday through Friday from 7 AM until 3:30 PM. Pay is based on experience, must have an updated resume. The associate will perform all soldering, bonding, wiring, routing, assembly, disassembly, touch-up, rework, cleaning, and minor modifications, assemblies and sub-assemblies within the facility using electronic parts and components and a variety of hand tools.

Payrate is 20 to 25 an hour depending on experience

The associate will work from approved visual aids, change notices (CN's), deviations and routes and/or any engineer-approved changes that apply to them. Solderers will also move the completed product to the next production operation. You will also use various measuring instruments and equipment to perform a visual and dimensional inspection of printed circuit boards, harnesses, sub-assemblies, and assemblies. Inspects assemblies after machine soldering and complete required paperwork, logs, and records.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
 
  • Perform manual and automated soldering of electronic components onto printed circuit boards
  • Read and interpret technical drawings, schematics, and work instructions
  • Set up and operate soldering equipment, including wave soldering machines and reflow ovens
  • Inspect solder joints and completed assemblies for quality and conformance to specifications
  • Clean and maintain soldering equipment and work area
REQUIREMENTS
  • Previous experience in electronic soldering, preferably in a manufacturing environment Ability to follow verbal and written instructions in English
  • Proficiency in various soldering techniques, including through-hole and surface mount technology Ability to identify electronic components
  • Ability to frequently lift/carry products weighing up to 50 lbs.
  • Ability to read and understand technical documents and schematics
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality
  • Good hand-eye coordination and manual dexterity
  • Good time management and organizational skills
OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES
  • Must complete soldering training course and pass soldering proficiency test
  • Ability to maintain hourly run rates in a fast-paced environment
  • Basic Math Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) training Electronic component identification training

job.title: Cloud Engineer
job.description:
Overview
The Cloud Engineer is responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining secure, scalable, and reliable cloud-based solutions. This role supports business objectives by optimizing cloud infrastructure, automating deployments, and ensuring compliance with security and performance standards.
The position works across enterprise and research application environments, helping Client build, operate, and continuously improve cloud platforms that are secure, resilient, cost-effective, and aligned with operational and compliance requirements.

Core Responsibilities
• Design and deploy cloud architectures across AWS and/or Azure that meet performance, security, availability, and cost-efficiency requirements.
• Architect and implement cloud networking, compute, storage, and identity services using least-privilege access, network segmentation, encryption, and defense-in-depth security principles.
• Evaluate and recommend cloud services, architectural patterns, and infrastructure approaches, balancing engineering capability, operational cost, and long-term platform sustainability.
• Implement and maintain infrastructure-as-code (IaC) solutions using Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible, or equivalent technologies.
• Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for cloud infrastructure and application deployments, including automated testing, validation, deployment, and rollback capabilities.
• Automate operational processes including patching, scaling, monitoring, alerting, and cost optimization to improve reliability and reduce manual effort.
• Ensure cloud environments comply with security standards, regulatory requirements, and data governance policies through controls for identity management, secrets management, audit logging, and encryption.
• Monitor cloud security posture, identify and remediate misconfigurations and policy violations, and integrate CSPM tooling into operational workflows.
• Partner with cybersecurity teams to align cloud security with enterprise threat models and regulatory frameworks, including GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, HIPAA, and SOX where applicable.
• Monitor cloud environments for performance, availability, and cost efficiency, applying FinOps practices and resource optimization strategies.
• Contribute to platform engineering standards, reference architectures, and guardrails that enable consistent and secure cloud adoption.
• Troubleshoot cloud infrastructure issues, participate in post-incident analysis, and implement preventive improvements to reduce recurrence.

Essential Qualifications, Skills, and Technologies
• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
• 3+ years of hands-on cloud engineering experience in a production enterprise environment with AWS and/or Azure.
• Demonstrated proficiency with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible, or equivalent, along with version control using Git.
• Proficiency in scripting languages such as Python, Bash, or equivalent for automation and tooling development.
• Strong understanding of cloud networking, virtualization, containerization technologies including Docker and Kubernetes, and cloud security principles.
• Experience building and supporting CI/CD pipelines and applying DevOps practices in cloud-native environments.

Preferred Skills or Experience
• AWS Certified Solutions Architect (Associate or Professional), AWS DevOps Engineer, Azure Administrator, Azure Architect, or related cloud certifications.
• Experience with FinOps practices and cloud cost optimization at enterprise scale.
• Familiarity with observability and monitoring platforms such as Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk, CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, or equivalent tools.
• Experience in pharmaceutical, healthcare, life sciences, or other regulated industries, including exposure to GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, or HIPAA cloud compliance requirements.
• Experience operating Kubernetes environments in production, including EKS, AKS, or self-managed clusters and workload management.
• Experience with Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) or Agent Reliability Engineering.
• Experience working in a fast-paced Agile environment.
• Background in cloud security architecture, including IAM design, secrets management, network security groups, and cloud-native security tooling.

job.title: Ansible Automation Engineer - (Active Secret Clearance Required)
job.description:
Overview
Client is seeking an Ansible Engineer to support infrastructure automation, configuration management, and operational consistency across Linux, Windows, containerized, and cloud-based environments. This role focuses on working on F-35 Pilot training devices, developing reusable automation solutions, integrating infrastructure tooling, and supporting secure, scalable deployment practices.
The ideal candidate will have strong expertise in Ansible, infrastructure-as-code concepts, systems administration, and automation testing, with experience integrating automation into modern CI/CD and observability platforms.

Core Responsibilities
• Design, develop, and maintain idempotent Ansible playbooks and reusable roles while managing role dependencies and automation standards.
• Create and manage static and dynamic inventories, host variables, and integrations with external inventory sources.
• Automate Linux and Windows system administration tasks, including package management, system configuration, PowerShell-based remediation, and Active Directory integration.
• Support infrastructure provisioning and post-provisioning configuration using Ansible in conjunction with tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation.
• Implement automation for containerized and Kubernetes environments, including cluster bootstrapping, deployment management, and runtime configuration.
• Integrate Ansible workflows into Git-based development processes, pull-request reviews, and CI/CD pipelines.
• Develop testing and validation frameworks using tools such as Molecule, TestInfra, and policy or schema validation solutions.
• Implement and maintain secure secrets management solutions using Ansible Vault, HashiCorp Vault, or cloud-based key management services.
• Support compliance initiatives by maintaining audit trails, generating compliance reporting, and ensuring automation aligns with organizational security standards.
• Integrate automation workflows with monitoring and observability platforms to improve operational visibility and detect configuration drift.

Essential Qualifications, Skills, and Technologies
• Strong experience developing Ansible playbooks and roles, including idempotent automation design, dependency management, and reusable role structures.
• Deep understanding of YAML and Jinja2, including templating, filters, conditionals, and dynamic configuration generation.
• Experience with inventory management, including host grouping, host variables, static inventories, dynamic inventories, and external inventory integrations.
• Strong Linux administration experience across distributions such as RHEL, Ubuntu, Debian, and Alpine.
• Experience supporting Windows environments using Ansible Windows modules, PowerShell, and Active Directory integrations.
• Knowledge of infrastructure automation and configuration management practices using Ansible and infrastructure-as-code tools.
• Experience with Kubernetes, container platforms, and automation of deployment and cluster management tasks.
• Proficiency with Git workflows, repository management, branching strategies, and pull-request-based review processes.
• Experience integrating automation into GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or Azure Pipelines, including automated testing and linting.
• Hands-on experience with Molecule, TestInfra, and automation testing methodologies.
• Experience implementing secrets management solutions using HashiCorp Vault, Ansible Vault, or cloud key management services.
• Understanding of compliance, auditing, and security-focused automation practices.
• Knowledge of networking fundamentals, including DNS, DHCP, VPCs, subnets, load balancers, firewalls, and IP address management.
• Scripting experience using Python or Bash for automation, custom modules, and tool integration.

Preferred Skills or Experience
• Familiarity with Terraform, Pulumi, or CloudFormation in hybrid or multi-cloud infrastructure environments.
• Experience integrating automation telemetry and operational data into Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, or Splunk environments.

Work Details
• Security Clearance Required: Secret.
• Work arrangement: Worker will telework less than 50% of the time.
• Schedule: 4/10, 1st Shift.
• Opportunity for full-time hire.
• Program supports F-35 pilot training devices under Prime Contract #N00019-19-C-0010.
• Access to ECI information is required.

job.title: Contracts Specialist, Discovery Sciences(Fully Remote)
job.description:
Contracts Specialist – Discovery Science / Life Sciences

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Contracts Specialist for a 6–12 month, full-time temporary assignment supporting discovery science and research contracting activities.

This individual contributor will be responsible for drafting, negotiating, and processing procurement-facing agreements supporting outsourced discovery science and research services. The Contracts Specialist will work from assignments provided by the contracting lead and will execute agreements accurately, efficiently, and within established templates, playbooks, approval frameworks, and systems.

The ideal candidate will have previous contracts experience within a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO, or life sciences procurement environment and be comfortable managing a high volume of agreements while negotiating directly with external suppliers.

Scope of Work

Contract Drafting & Negotiation

  • Draft, review, negotiate, and finalize assigned agreements for outsourced discovery science services.

  • Manage agreements including:

    • Confidentiality Agreements (CDAs)

    • Work Orders

    • Amendments

    • Software and SaaS Agreements

  • Negotiate directly with third-party suppliers to advance and close assigned agreements.

  • Apply established contract templates, fallback positions, playbooks, and approval frameworks throughout the negotiation process.

  • Review agreements for common commercial and legal provisions, including:

    • Intellectual Property

    • Confidentiality

    • Indemnification

    • Limitation of Liability

    • Payment Terms

Contract Management & Compliance

  • Manage a high volume of concurrent contract assignments while meeting established timelines.

  • Adjust priorities as directed by the contracting lead.

  • Identify non-standard terms, contractual risks, or issues that fall outside established playbook positions.

  • Escalate identified issues to the contracting lead with a clear summary of the concern and proposed options.

  • Provide regular status updates regarding assigned agreements.

Contract Lifecycle Management

  • Utilize the organization's Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) system for all assigned work.

  • Manage contract activities within the CLM system, including:

    • Intake

    • Drafting

    • Version Control

    • Status Tracking

    • Record Keeping

  • Maintain complete, current, and accurate contract records.

Procurement Support

  • Create purchase requisitions in SAP Ariba for executed agreements as assigned.

Out of Scope

This position will not be responsible for:

  • Engaging directly with internal business partners, scientific teams, or project management teams regarding contracting needs or intake.

  • Escalating matters directly to Legal or other internal subject matter experts. All escalations will be routed through the contracting lead.

  • Procure-to-pay activities beyond purchase requisition creation.

  • Invoice reconciliation.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree.

  • 2+ years of contract drafting and negotiation experience within a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO, or life sciences procurement environment.

  • Working knowledge of common commercial and legal contract provisions, including:

    • Intellectual Property

    • Confidentiality

    • Indemnification

    • Limitation of Liability

    • Payment Terms

  • Demonstrated ability to manage a high volume of concurrent agreements while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.

  • Experience working within established contract templates, playbooks, and approval frameworks.

  • Experience using a Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) system.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Experience negotiating directly with external suppliers.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including:

    • Outlook

    • Word

    • Excel

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience contracting for outsourced research and discovery science services, including:

    • Preclinical CRO services

    • Discovery Biology

    • Chemistry Services

  • Degree or professional background in biology or another related scientific discipline.

  • Scientific literacy sufficient to understand the scope, deliverables, and technical terminology associated with discovery research services, including:

    • In vitro studies

    • In vivo studies

    • Assay development

    • Chemistry services

  • Ability to accurately translate scientific and technical requirements into contract language.

  • Experience negotiating software and SaaS agreements, including data platform agreements within a research environment.

  • Experience with SAP Ariba or a comparable procurement platform.

  • Comfortable using AI tools to support contract drafting and review.

Key Skills

  • Contract Drafting & Negotiation

  • Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)

  • Pharmaceutical / Biotechnology Contracting

  • CRO & Research Services Agreements

  • Supplier Negotiations

  • Confidentiality Agreements (CDAs)

  • Work Orders & Amendments

  • Software / SaaS Agreements

  • Commercial & Legal Terms

  • Risk Identification & Escalation

  • SAP Ariba

  • High-Volume Contract Management

  • Microsoft Office

  • Attention to Detail

Work Environment

  • Assignment Length: 6–12 months

  • Schedule: Full-time

  • Travel: None expected

job.title: Technical Editor I
job.description:
Job Description:
Contractor, Nonclinical Document Management & Workflow Support

Role Overview:
The contractor will provide essential support for document lifecycle management, data entry, and workflow coordination for nonclinical documents supporting various regulatory submission types. This role focuses on ensuring document accuracy, maintaining organized digital libraries, and collaborating across functional groups. The contractor will work closely with Submission Managers and serve as a resource to project and submission teams (such as Pharmacology Subteams) to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality, compliant documents that meet global regulatory standards.

Key Responsibilities:
Document Management & Processing:
Build familiarity with internal processes, tools, and document management systems, seeking guidance from experienced submission managers as needed.
Transfer and manage documents across various digital libraries and folder structures.
Accurately capture, identify, and apply metadata to files and system records.
Publish finalized documents and reports within the document management system.
Quality Control & Editing:
Perform quality control (QC) and verification of documents to ensure they meet readiness standards.
Format, edit, and track nonclinical documents (e.g., nonclinical study reports, GLP statements, CRO reports, IND/BLA summaries), applying established editorial standards and templates to ensure accuracy, completeness, and internal consistency.
Retrieve missing information by searching through historical archives and tracking down data.
System Workflow & Coordination:
Initiate document records within the tracking and document management systems.
Enter system data and accurately match documents to broader project plans.
Assess and develop timelines for document deliverables, supporting authors by tracking the completion of documents.
Manage collaborations by coordinating document hand-offs and review cycles between subject matter experts, authors, publishing teams, and stakeholders in Development Sciences, Regulatory Affairs, and other functions.
Identify problems with documents or submissions and collaborate with the team to develop effective solutions.
Internal Communications & Content Management:
Manage and maintain internal team websites or portals.
Create new content and perform routine updates to ensure information remains current.
Serve as an editorial contact and communicate documentation processes to team members and stakeholders.

Qualifications:
Education:
B.A./B.S. degree in English, science, communications, liberal arts, or a health-related field.

Experience:
Minimum of 2 years of scientific editing, writing, or document management experience.

Skills:
Knowledge of the drug development process and regulatory submissions is mandatory.
Strong project management and organizational skills is mandatory .
Ability to anticipate and solve issues impacting timelines.
Ability to work concurrently on multiple projects, meet aggressive deadlines, and contribute effectively in a fast-paced, highly collaborative team environment.
Strong written and verbal communication, solutions-focused mindset.
High attention to detail to prevent inaccurate or substandard documents that could lead to submission corrections or delays.
Experience leveraging AI-augmented tools and automation to streamline documentation workflows and enhance overall efficiency is preferred.
Profiency with MS Word

job.title: Locomotive Mechanic
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced Senior Locomotive Mechanic / Electrician for a hands-on role supporting diesel-electric locomotives and railroad equipment throughout the field and shop environment.

This is not a trainee position. We're looking for a journeyman-level mechanic who can independently diagnose and repair complex mechanical, electrical, and air-brake systems, work with limited supervision, and serve as a technical resource to other mechanics.

The position is based in Baytown, TX, with significant travel throughout the country. Candidates who enjoy field work, troubleshooting complex equipment, and working on different locomotive units are encouraged to apply.

What You'll Do

  • Inspect, diagnose, repair, and maintain diesel-electric locomotives and railroad equipment.
  • Troubleshoot complex mechanical, electrical, and air-brake systems.
  • Work on EMD and Client locomotives, including running repairs and major component work.
  • Troubleshoot locomotive control systems, wiring, batteries, charging systems, traction systems, and high-current electrical components.
  • Perform and lead engine, truck, brake, and major-component repairs and overhauls.
  • Inspect and repair safety-critical locomotive systems and document defects and corrective actions.
  • Read and interpret wiring diagrams, schematics, locomotive drawings, work orders, and parts information.
  • Test completed repairs, perform load checks, and assist with locomotive operation prior to return to service.
  • Use electrical meters, hand tools, cutting torches, welders, forklifts, and other shop equipment.
  • Maintain accurate records of inspections, repairs, parts, labor, and required documentation.
  • Help train and mentor less-experienced mechanics and electricians.
  • Coordinate with supervisors, train crews, and customers regarding equipment status, repair timelines, and parts requirements.
  • Identify repeat equipment failures, parts shortages, and other maintenance issues.
  • Follow all company and customer safety requirements.
  • Travel and work away from your home area, including overnight assignments.
  • Work nights, weekends, overtime, and irregular schedules when required.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 5 years of hands-on experience repairing diesel-electric locomotives or closely related diesel-electric/heavy power-generation equipment.
  • Working knowledge of EMD and/or Client locomotive systems.
  • Strong mechanical and electrical troubleshooting ability.
  • Experience with locomotive electrical systems, diesel prime movers, and air-brake systems.
  • Ability to diagnose equipment problems independently without step-by-step direction.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, work orders, and locomotive drawings.
  • Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record.
  • Ability to pass a pre-employment background check and drug screen.
  • Ability to complete required safety training.
  • Willingness and ability to travel overnight up to five days per week.
  • Willingness to work irregular hours, nights, weekends, and overtime as required.

Related Experience Considered

Candidates without five years specifically on locomotives may be considered if they have significant experience with comparable diesel-electric, heavy equipment, marine, or industrial power-generation systems, particularly where the work involved high-voltage/high-current electrical systems and diesel prime movers.

Locomotive experience is strongly preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

  • EMD locomotive experience
  • Client locomotive experience
  • Welding experience
  • Cutting-torch experience
  • Forklift experience
  • Prior experience training or mentoring mechanics
  • Previous technical lead experience
  • Railroad or heavy-equipment maintenance background

Important: This Is a Working Technical Role

Although this is a Senior position, it does not automatically include formal supervisory authority.

You will be expected to take technical ownership of assigned work, help set the quality and safety standard for the crew, and provide guidance to less-experienced mechanics.

Physical & Work Environment

This is a hands-on mechanical/electrical position performed in locomotive shops and outdoor field environments.

The job may involve:

  • Standing, walking, climbing, balancing, bending, kneeling, crouching, and crawling.
  • Working around moving railroad equipment.
  • Exposure to weather, vibration, noise, fumes, oils, grease, and airborne particles.
  • Working around live electrical systems and potential electrical-shock hazards.
  • Working at heights.
  • Regularly lifting or moving up to 25 pounds and frequently lifting or moving up to 100 pounds with assistance when required.
  • Use of required PPE and hearing protection.

Color vision is required for electrical work.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity for an experienced locomotive mechanic/electrician to take on a senior-level technical role with significant field exposure.

If you're currently working as a locomotive mechanic, locomotive electrician, diesel mechanic, railroad mechanic, heavy-equipment mechanic, or industrial power-generation technician and are comfortable traveling for work, we'd like to speak with you.

Apply today to be considered for this opportunity.

Keywords: Locomotive Mechanic, Senior Locomotive Mechanic, Locomotive Electrician, Locomotive Technician, Diesel Mechanic, Diesel-Electric Mechanic, Railroad Mechanic, Railroad Technician, EMD Mechanic, Client Locomotive Mechanic, Heavy Equipment Mechanic, Diesel Technician, Power Generation Technician, Field Service Technician, Railroad Maintenance, Locomotive Maintenance.

job.title: Optical Measurements Engineer
job.description:
Optical Measurements Systems Engineer

Location: Painted Post, NY – Onsite
Schedule: 40+ hours per week
Pay Range: $43.01–$55.62/hour
Work Authorization: US Citizen or US Permanent Resident (Green Card Holder)

Position Summary

We are seeking an Optical Measurements Systems Engineer to join the Corning Environmental Technologies (CET) Engineering Measurements & Controls group. This engineer will be responsible for the development, assembly, testing, integration, and deployment of optical and computer vision-based measurement systems supporting the metrology, inspection, and testing of CET products.

The position will work closely with cross-functional teams and external suppliers to transition measurement technologies from early-stage development into reliable manufacturing systems.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement optical and computer vision-based measurement and instrumentation systems.
  • Collaborate with Development, Quality, IT, Purchasing, and Operations teams to define system requirements and solutions.
  • Transfer technology from development into manufacturing.
  • Partner with external suppliers and system integrators to implement key technologies.
  • Develop scopes of work, obtain competitive quotes, issue purchase orders, track supplier activities, and approve invoices.
  • Design experiments and analyze data to improve measurement systems and production processes.
  • Create and maintain production documentation, including machine specifications, operating procedures, and drawing packages.
  • Train engineering, maintenance, and operations personnel on the use and maintenance of measurement systems.
  • Provide onsite and remote troubleshooting using system performance data and analysis.
  • Support system checkout, installation, integration, and deployment.

Required Qualifications

  • BS or MS degree in Optics, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or Computer Engineering with 3+ years of hands-on experience with machine vision and metrology equipment; OR
  • PhD in one of the above disciplines.
  • Hands-on experience with vision systems is required.
  • Experience developing optical measurement systems involving cameras, lighting, image acquisition, image analysis, lasers, and/or 3D measurement.
  • Fundamental understanding of physical optics.
  • Knowledge of image-processing techniques such as blob analysis, edge finding, morphology, feature extraction, classification, and metrology.
  • Experience with Microsoft Visual Studio; C# and Python strongly preferred.
  • Experience with systems engineering and integration.
  • Knowledge of digital signal processing.
  • Experience with electrical, optical, and mechanical installations, system checkout, and troubleshooting.
  • Strong communication, presentation, and Microsoft Office skills.
  • Experience retrieving, plotting, and analyzing data, primarily using Microsoft Excel.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Halcon, Matrox Inspector, NI Vision, Cognex, Keyence, or MATLAB Image Processing Toolbox.
  • PLC and control systems experience.
  • Process engineering experience, including DOE, statistical analysis, and process improvement.
  • Experience with manufacturing metrology, inspection, and product quality.
  • Motion-control integration for imaging platforms.
  • Experience with high-performance computing systems.
  • Experience with 3D transformations, topography, point clouds, surface meshes, and 3D registration.
  • Experience developing automated 3D metrology and inspection solutions.
  • Familiarity with machine learning and deep learning theory.
  • Experience designing or deploying machine learning/deep learning models.

What We're Looking For

The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineer with strong experience in machine vision, optical measurement systems, image processing, metrology, and systems integration. The successful candidate will be comfortable working across engineering and manufacturing environments, troubleshooting complex systems, analyzing data, and transitioning new technologies into production.

Strong communication skills, independence, adaptability, problem-solving ability, and the ability to manage multiple priorities are essential.

Work Authorization: Candidates must be a US Citizen or US Permanent Resident (Green Card Holder).

job.title: Quality Engineer
job.description:
Quality Engineer

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain and continuously improve the Quality Management System (QMS).
  • Manage the internal audit process to ensure QMS compliance.
  • Create, collect, analyze, and maintain company performance metrics, including on-time delivery, non-conformances, and supplier defects; report results to the broader organization.
  • Ensure inspection and quality-control equipment meets required standards and recommend improvements to procedures, processes, standards, and equipment.
  • Compile and maintain inspection reports and quality records.
  • Perform root-cause analysis, collaborate with Engineering, and advise other departments on corrective measures.
  • Develop and implement corrective and preventive action plans to address quality issues and prevent recurrence.
  • Interface with customer and government quality representatives regarding audits, corrective actions, acceptance testing, and other quality-related matters.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure quality standards are met throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Support quality inspections to ensure the efficient processing of parts and maintain manufacturing production lines.
  • Develop, maintain, and deploy quality plans and activities that translate customer requirements into actionable quality requirements.
  • Analyze quality program requirements and prepare quality plans, procedures, and schedules to ensure effective quality support and compliance.
  • Provide training and guidance to team members on quality-control procedures and best practices.
  • Maintain documentation and records related to quality-control activities.
  • Ensure compliance with Quality Management System procedures.
  • Perform other duties as requested, directed, or assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.
  • 3–5 years of experience in Quality Engineering or Quality Management.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Ability to read and interpret complex technical drawings.
  • Excellent communication skills.
  • Self-starter who can work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Must be a U.S. Person or a non-U.S. Person eligible to obtain any required Export Authorization.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with inspection, quality control, and quality assurance methods, techniques, and equipment.
  • Familiarity with AS9100/ISO 9100 requirements.
  • Knowledge of statistical quality-control techniques.
  • Experience using a variety of measuring instruments.

Physical Requirements

  • Must successfully pass a vision examination, including near vision and color vision if required, as a condition of employment and/or periodically thereafter.
  • Ability to read small text and handwriting.
  • Manual dexterity and ability to perform repetitive tasks.
  • Frequently required to stand.
  • Ability to visually examine parts and documents.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds.

job.title: Machine Operator
job.description:
Position Summary

Join a dynamic team where you will be responsible for safely operating, monitoring, and maintaining production equipment to meet output, quality, and safety standards. This role offers an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced manufacturing environment, where your strong attention to detail and mechanical awareness will be highly valued.

Key Responsibilities

Machine Operation

  • Set up, operate, and adjust production equipment including filling, blending, packaging, or assembly machines.
  • Monitor machine performance and make real-time adjustments to maintain efficiency.
  • Perform changeovers based on product specifications.
  • Ensure proper material loading and product flow.

Production & Output

  • Meet or exceed daily production targets.
  • Minimize downtime by identifying and addressing minor issues quickly.
  • Accurately complete production counts and documentation.

Quality Control

  • Inspect product to ensure it meets quality standards.
  • Identify defects and escalate issues immediately.
  • Follow GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices) and sanitation procedures.

Safety & Compliance

  • Follow all safety procedures and wear required PPE.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work area according to 5S standards.
  • Report safety hazards, near misses, and incidents.

Maintenance Support

  • Perform basic preventative maintenance including cleaning, lubrication, and inspections.
  • Assist the maintenance team with troubleshooting when needed.
  • Identify early signs of equipment failure.

Qualifications

Required

  • 1 year of manufacturing or machine operation experience.
  • Ability to stand for extended periods and lift up to 50 lbs.
  • Basic mechanical aptitude.

Preferred

  • Experience with packaging equipment such as HFFS, fillers, cappers, conveyors.
  • Familiarity with GMP or regulated manufacturing environments.
  • Forklift certification or willingness to obtain.

Key Skills & Traits

  • Strong work ethic and reliability, with critical attendance.
  • Hands-on problem solver.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Sense of urgency and accountability.
  • Willingness to learn and grow.

Work Environment

  • Manufacturing floor with noise, moving equipment, and chemicals depending on the area.
  • Exposure to dust, powder, and liquid cleaning chemicals.
  • Exposure to ambient temperature, hot in summer and cold in winter.
  • Shift: Monday-Thursday, 6:00 AM-4:30 PM, with overtime as needed.

job.title: Material Processor ll
job.description:
Overview:

Daifuku Automotive America Corporation is a leader in optimizing, integrating, automating, and managing the logistical flow of material goods in the automotive automation/material handling systems. We focus on Design, Manufacturing, Installation and Support. Daifuku America Corporation has been a trusted partner to some of the world's largest and fastest-growing companies, showing them how to use their space more efficiently to deliver improved productivity.

The company is currently seeking an experienced Material Processor I I for our facility in Reynoldsburg, OH.

Daifuku Automotive America Corporation promotes and supports both individual and team success by providing opportunities to expand your skills and build on your capabilities. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we are committed to a culturally rich workforce and proud of our diversity in background, experience and origin. Safety is part of our core values; we stress the importance to our employees by enforcing 5S and daily safety audits.

Daifuku Benefits

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision available day one
  • Optional Critical Illness and Accident Insurance
  • FSA/ HSA
  • Company provided life and disability plans
  • 401K: Fidelity
  • 7 Paid sick days (prorated according to start date)
  • 13 paid vacation days (prorated according to start date)
  • 11 paid holidays
  • Yearly performance bonuses
  • PPE Reimbursement

Responsibilities:

The primary goal is satisfying customer requirements of quality, quantity, and delivery, in a safe manner, while maximizing productivity. Specifically, the Material Processor I I is responsible for all job activities required to support production processes. These activities include but are not limited to: Machine operation, cutting, sawing, drilling, tapping, grinding parts, prepping kits, and Client-outs to meet our customer specifications. Employee is responsible for visually inspecting parts.

Other responsibilities:

  • Follows all plant safety guidelines, practices and procedures. Also, be aware of activity in the work surroundings and maintain a clean and safe work area
  • Properly use personal protective equipment when required
  • Maintain regular attendance – have reliable means of transportation
  • Perform other tasks as assigned

Qualifications:

Prior manufacturing experience is highly preferred. Any technical or vocational education/training in relation to skills listed below is also desirable.

  • Must have intermediate blueprint reading knowledge and the ability to follow the work order instructions
  • Ability to properly use material processing tools and machines such as drill presses, punches, saws, and layout tools.
  • Forklift, overhead crane and man lift experience preferred (in-house training available)
  • Must be able to pass a background check and pre employment drug test
  • Team player - must be able to communicate and work with others
  • Must have and maintain a high sense of urgency to meet and exceed all production goals
  • Attentive to detail watching for material defects and any quality issues.
  • Physically capable of standing, walking, bending, pushing, pulling, reaching and twisting throughout shift
  • Capable of repetitively lifting 25-50 lbs.
  • Candidates must be flexible to work overtime as needed, which may include weekends and/or holidays

Work Environment

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee works in typical manufacturing environment with overhead cranes and forklifts.
  • Overhead LED lights throughout the workspace create a bright workspace for employees to safely perform their work.
  • Normally clean work environment where the process creates some grinding dust, heat/cold, fumes/odors, and vibration. Housekeeping is performed as needed throughout the day and at the end of each shift.
  • The noise level in the work environment is normal to manufacturing processes with air tools, grinders, and other tools. Yearly audiometric testing is provided by the company to monitor areas for improvement.
  • Non-climate-controlled facility in the summer, each work area is provided with fans to help keep cool. In the winter it is heated.

 

Education and Experience
High School Diploma or equivalent

1-3 experience processing material in a manufacturing environment

Prior machine operation experience desirable

Required Equipment

Steel Toe Shoes/Boots

Basic tools

COM068

job.title: Sheet Metal Model Maker
job.description:
Sheet Metal Model Maker

Direct Hire
Macomb County, MI

Basic Function

To transform blueprints, digital plans, or abstract concepts into accurate, physical three-dimensional representations or prototypes using a variety of materials and tools.

  • Prototype Fabrication: Cut, form, bend, and assemble high-precision prototype sheet metal components from various materials (e.g., steel, aluminum, stainless steel).

  • Blueprint & CAD Interpretation: Read and interpret complex engineering blueprints, 3D CAD models, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), and technical sketches.

  • Equipment Operation: Set up and safely operate a variety of manufacturing equipment, including laser cutters, press brakes, shears, rollers, manual mills, lathes, and drill presses.

  • Layout & Development: Perform flat pattern layouts and calculate bend allowances to determine exact material requirements for development.

  • Assembly & Joining: Fit and assemble components using welding (TIG/MIG), spot welding, brazing, riveting, or mechanical fasteners.

  • Quality Inspection: Inspect finished prototype parts using precision measuring instruments (calipers, micrometers, height gauges, CMM) to ensure adherence to strict tolerances.

  • Design Collaboration: Work closely with product design and manufacturing engineers to provide feedback on prototype performance, material behavior, and design for manufacturability (DFM).

  • Tooling & Fixtures: Design and fabricate temporary shop tooling, jigs, and fixtures required to produce prototype parts efficiently.


Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Technical Expertise: Advanced proficiency in sheet metal fabrication techniques, layout, development, and material properties.

  •  Equipment Proficiency: Demonstrated experience operating standard fabrication machinery (press brakes, shears) and manual machine shop tools.

  • Blueprint Reading: Strong capability in reading technical drawings and a solid understanding of GD&T principles.

  • Precision Measurement: Skilled in using precision inspection tools to verify parts against engineering specifications.

  • Mathematical Skills: Strong shop math skills, including trigonometry and geometry, for flat-pattern development and bend calculations.

  • Problem-Solving: Ability to troubleshoot fitment or fabrication issues on the fly and suggest practical design modifications.


Preferred Qualifications

  • CAD/CAM Skills: Experience using CAD software (SolidWorks, Autodesk Inventor) or CAM software for CNC programming.

  • Welding Certification: Certified or highly proficient in TIG and MIG welding for thin-gauge sheet metal.

Education & Training

  • Education: High School Diploma or equivalent.

  • Training: Completion of Vocational Training in Machining or Metal Fabrication preferred.

  • Experience: Prior experience in industrial fabrication and machining, specifically within a prototype or tool & die setting.

job.title: Machine Operator
job.description:
Machine Operator Job Description

Job Title: Machine Operator

Department: Production / Operations

Reports To: Production Supervisor / Operations Manager

Location: Elyria, Ohio

Job Type: Full-Time [Shift: 1st / 2nd / 3rd Shift]

Job Summary

We are seeking a reliable and detail-oriented Machine Operator to join our production team in Elyria, Ohio . In this role, you will be responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining industrial machinery to manufacture high-quality products according to specifications. The ideal candidate has strong mechanical aptitude, places a high priority on safety, and works well in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Machine Operation: Set up, calibrate, and operate equipment [e.g., CNC machines, press brakes, extruders, stamping presses, packaging machinery] according to production schedules and specifications.

  • Quality Control: Inspect raw materials and finished parts using precision measuring tools [e.g., calipers, micrometers, gauges] to ensure they meet quality standards and engineering drawings.

  • Setup & Adjustments: Adjust machine settings, tooling, feeds, and speeds to optimize efficiency and product accuracy.

  • Routine Maintenance: Perform basic preventive maintenance, cleaning, and lubrication on assigned machines; troubleshoot minor operational issues.

  • Safety & Compliance: Adhere strictly to company safety protocols, OSHA guidelines, Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements, and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures.

  • Documentation: Maintain accurate production logs, material tracking, scrap counts, and quality control reports.

  • Team Collaboration: Communicate effectively with shift supervisors, quality assurance teams, and maintenance staff to keep operations running smoothly.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • Education: High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent vocational training.

  • Experience: [1–3+] years of experience operating machinery in a manufacturing or industrial setting preferred.

  • Technical Skills:

    • Ability to read blueprints, work instructions, and technical documentation.

    • Familiarity with standard measuring devices [calipers, micrometers, tape measures] .

    • Basic shop math and basic computer entry skills.

  • Physical Requirements:

    • Ability to stand, bend, reach, and lift up to [50 lbs] periodically throughout an 8- to 12-hour shift.

    • Good hand-eye coordination, manual dexterity, and close-up visual acuity.

  • Work Ethic: High attention to detail, strong punctuality, safety-first mindset, and ability to work effectively in a team environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in automotive, metal fabrication, plastics, or heavy manufacturing equipment.

  • Valid Forklift / Material Handling Certification.

  • Prior experience with [specific machine brand/controller, e.g., Haas, Fanuc, Allen-Bradley] .

job.title: NDT Inspector II
job.description:
Job Description Breakdown

Position: NDT Inspector II – Direct Hire
Industry: Aerospace / Engine Components
Pay: $27–$32/hr, depending on experience
Employment: Direct Hire / RPO
Location: Not provided

Openings / Shifts:

  • 1st Shift: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM — 1 opening
  • 2nd Shift: Monday–Friday, 2:00 PM–10:00 PM — 1 opening
  • 3rd Shift: Sunday night–Friday morning, 10:00 PM–6:00 AM — 1 opening

What They're Looking For

The NDT Inspector II will perform Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) on commercial and military aircraft engine accessories, as well as land and marine engine accessories.

The primary inspection methods are:

  • Digital Radiography (RT/X-ray)
  • Fluorescent Penetrant Testing (PT/FPI)

Ideally, candidates will have experience with both RT and PT, but candidates with experience in only one method may still be considered. Candidates with only one method may be considered at the lower end of the pay range, depending on overall experience.

Key Responsibilities

  • Inspect hardware using approved NDT methods to ensure quality requirements are met.
  • Set up and calibrate NDT equipment.
  • Perform inspections and interpret/evaluate results.
  • Document inspection results in accordance with approved procedures.
  • Develop techniques/work instructions for digital RT and PT under Level III approval.
  • Understand applicable codes, standards, specifications and contractual requirements.
  • Provide guidance and/or supervision to Level I personnel and trainees.
  • Perform failure analysis, product development, R&D and production inspections.
  • Perform digital RT and CT inspections.
  • Reconstruct and compile inspection data.
  • Flex between NDT methods based on business needs.

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma/GED or higher.
  • Must currently meet NAS-410 qualification requirements.
  • Must be eligible to certify as an NDT Level II in Radiographic Testing and Penetrant Testing.
  • Minimum documented experience/training:
    • Radiographic Testing: 1,600 hours of work experience + 80 hours formal training
    • Penetrant Testing/FPI: 400 hours of work experience + 32 hours formal training
  • Must pass required general, specific and practical examinations.
  • Must achieve required scores for Parker's Level II certification.
  • Must pass 20/25 near-vision examination at 16" ± 1" and color deficiency testing.
  • U.S. Citizen or U.S. Permanent Resident required.
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills.

Preferred / Nice-to-Have

  • Welding experience/knowledge
  • Heat treating and brazing knowledge
  • Machining experience
  • Assembly experience
  • FAA Repair Station experience
  • Experience with both RT and PT
  • Digital radiography / CT experience

Key Recruiter Screening Item

Notes about the role: we do both X-ray (radiographic) and PT (penetrant testing) within our NDT department. Ideally, candidates will have some experience in both areas, but we are open to talking to those who maybe only have one or other, they will just be on the low end of the pay rate, maybe a little under depending on years of experience. One thing we do request of all candidates and will need to view before setting up a call will be their OJT records to confirm the number of hours experience they have. Since this is an industry standard, this is something they should hopefully be able to supply.

Candidates should provide their OJT/training records so the team can verify their documented NDT hours, particularly:

  • RT hours
  • PT/FPI hours
  • Formal training hours
  • Certification/qualification history

This is especially important because the experience requirements are tied to NAS-410 qualification standards.


U.S. Citizenship or U.S. Permanent Resident status required.
